correctness.rationale: For every N≥4, character orthogonality invertibly transforms the complex measurement map into independent Fourier-difference bands. Its zero band recovers all N−1 diagonal entries via the deletion sum divided by N−2; a nonzero band recovers its sum via division by N−3, after which the residual data solve x_j+x_{j+δ}=b_j with x_0=x_δ=0. On an r-cycle, the homogeneous equation has no solution except zero if r is odd and one alternating degree if r is even. The cycle through zero is forced to vanish; the other N/r−1 even cycles are independent and have zero total, giving the exact kernel formula. Hermitian projector span has the same complex and real rank. Odd-order full Gram recovery and explicit even-order two-frequency phase ambiguities prove the iff corollary; N=2,3 are handled separately. The actual accompanying verify.py used standard-library exact rational elimination on twenty group presentations, tested every predicted even-band kernel vector, checked twenty random Gram reconstructions for each odd presentation, and replayed successfully. Independent numerical complex-projector ranks also agreed on eight test groups. Finite tests are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The publicly indexed cyclic frequency-deletion result already settles the yes/no phase-retrieval question for cyclic groups and explicitly excludes noncyclic groups, while Bartusel--Führ--Oussa treats the prime-order case. The new claim is not that covered yes/no assertion: it derives exact complex projector-span ranks and all missing matrix bands for every finite abelian group, including structure-dependent noncyclic even-order ranks. A detailed reading of the closest cyclic proof shows its recurrence mechanism but no even-order nullspace enumeration or matrix-rank theorem. Direct scientific searches for aliases and broader rank/tomography claims revealed no formula implying the element-order sum. Residual bibliographic risk remains.

value.rationale: The number of independent matrix observables of a deterministic frequency-deletion intensity frame is a natural quantitative tomography invariant that controls exact recovery of mixed states, whereas an ordinary phase-retrieval theorem addresses only rank-one uniqueness. The theorem gives every missing operator direction, not merely a sufficient criterion, and exhibits a pronounced structure transition between groups of the same size: ranks 44,36,28 for Z8, Z4×Z2, and Z2³. These rank deficits are motivated directly by finite Fourier measurement geometry and are not implied by the published odd-cyclic phase-retrieval existence theorem. No unproved noise-stability or broader theorem is asserted.
